title: Compliance Analyst - AI Governance
text:
About AlphaSense: 

AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com. Come join us.
About the Role:

The AI Governance Analyst is central to building and operating AlphaSense’s AI governance program, helping ensure that the way we deploy, build, and procure AI systems is well-governed, well-documented, and defensible to regulators, auditors, and enterprise clients. Sitting within the Strategic Risk team, this role owns the day-to-day execution of AI risk assessments — intake, classification, evaluation, and documentation — that keep the program running at scale.

As AlphaSense matures its governance infrastructure, including the rollout of a dedicated GRC platform to automate assessment workflows, this role acts as the operational backbone of the program: turning frameworks such as the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO/IEC 42001 into repeatable, auditable processes that grow with the business. This is a risk and governance role — not a hands-on AI engineering role — well-suited to someone who understands how AI systems create risk and knows how to manage it.

What You’ll Do:

Complete AI risk assessments using established templates and criteria — gathering details on AI use cases, working through classification and control questions, and preparing draft assessments for senior review.

Maintain the accuracy of the AI system inventory by adding and updating records of AI/ML systems, vendors, and use cases.

Leverage the AI governance platform to enter assessment data, follow set workflows, and organize supporting evidence and documentation.

Gather the information and evidence needed to map use cases against frameworks such as the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO/IEC 42001, with guidance on interpretation from senior team members.

Coordinate with engineering, product, security, legal and privacy, and procurement contacts to collect the details needed for assessments, and flag open questions for review.

Assist with third-party and vendor AI risk reviews by collecting vendor documentation and completing initial reviews for senior validation.

Draft clear, well-organized summaries and notes from completed assessments, and flag higher-risk or unclear items to senior reviewers.

Track the status of assessments and follow-ups, keeping records and trackers up to date so nothing slips through.

Who You Are:

IAPP AIGP certified with a strong knowledge of the AI governance landscape and the major frameworks shaping it.

2–4 years of experience in risk management, GRC, compliance, audit, or data privacy, with exposure to AI governance, technology risk, or third-party risk. 

Familiar with the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and ISO/IEC 27001, and able to apply their requirements to real use cases rather than just cite them.

Comfortable working with GRC or governance tooling — configuring workflows, managing inventories, and generating reporting — and quick to learn new platforms.

AI-literate without being a developer: able to understand at a conceptual level how AI and ML systems work, the risks they introduce (bias, hallucination, data leakage, model drift, and similar), and how to translate that

text:
Manufacturing Operations Engineer

Description -
Job Summary
 • This role focuses on designing engineering solutions for manufacturing processes, adhering to established principles and specifications. It involves implementing production standards, tooling requirements, and capacity models for new product components. The position includes collaborating with stakeholders to evaluate factory performance, communicating with internal and external partners on compliance and issues, and contributing to project teams for cost-effective manufacturing solutions. The role also ensures regulatory compliance and contributes to current-state analysis and recommendations while following company policies.
 
 Responsibilities

 • Implements and executes established time standards, production area layouts, and requirements for manufacturing tooling and processes for subsystems and portions of new products.

 • Develops and reviews key indicators to measure factory performance and provide recommendations to factory management.
 • Collaborates and communicates with management, internal, and outsourced manufacturing and development partners regarding processes, standards, compliance and manufacturing issues of existing products.

 • Participates as a member of project team of other manufacturing engineers and internal and outsourced manufacturing partners to develop and execute reliable, cost effective and high quality manufacturing solutions for low to moderately- complex products from new-product introduction through end of lifecycle.
 • Ensures compliance of manufacturing operations with necessary internal and external regulations.
 • Develops conclusions and written reports capturing current-state analysis and recommendations, contributing proactively through research and data analysis support.
 • Works independently on moderate scope problems, applying professional expertise, exercising judgment by following company policies and procedures.

Pay: $80–95/hour
Duration: Short-term pilot — approximately 2–3 weeks
Project kickoff:Ideally end of week( November 8th)
Location: Fully remote
You’ll need: PhD or PhD candidate in electrical, mechanical, chemical, industrial, or aerospace engineering
Your tasks: Build technical problems from real engineering workflows and define what makes an answer correct
This is a short pilot, roughly 2–3 weeks, focused on real engineering workflows: the problems you’d actually encounter in your research or practice, not textbook exercises. You’ll build those problems, provide the correct analysis, and define what separates a right answer from one that only looks right.

Design technical problems drawn from real engineering work in your field, with realistic constraints and supporting data.

Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.

Define objective criteria for correctness, so another engineer reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.

Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.

Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.

What we’re looking for

PhD, or PhD candidate, in electrical, mechanical, chemical, industrial, or aerospace engineering.

Degree from a strong research institution is preferred.

Hands-on research or practice experience — problems you worked on yourself, not ones you read about.

Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another engineer could verify it.

Publications or a record of technical contribution is a plus.

AI or LLM evaluation experience is a plus, but not required.

The Associate Software Development Engineer role at Swiggy is the entry point into our engineering team for high-potential builders who are not yet at the SDE I level but have already shown they can ship. We solve consumer problems and build new products at scale by leveraging modern engineering and AI tools, and we are looking for candidates who bring strong computer science fundamentals, high curiosity, high energy, and very high ownership.

What you will be expected to have is proof that you build things: PoCs, AI experiments, hackathon projects, side projects, or other hands-on work that you can demo and talk about in depth. As an ASDE, you will learn what it takes to turn an idea or experiment into a production-ready system, working alongside engineers who do this every day.
